paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: ask the LORD every time, even when you think you already know the answer. David faced the same enemy in the same valley, and he still inquired of the LORD again (2 Samuel 5:19, 23). The first time the answer was "Go up," and the second time it was "Do not march straight up, but circle around behind them." Same problem, brand new plan.

Think about what David could have done. He had a win in his pocket, and a win makes you feel like an expert. It's like finding one recipe that worked and never checking the oven again. David didn't run on yesterday's answer. He asked, he waited, and then he "did as the LORD had commanded him" (2 Samuel 5:25).

So here's what this means for you, baker. Yesterday's guidance doesn't replace today's asking. When the same old trouble shows up again, like a snooze alarm going off one more time, you don't have to guess how it goes. You can bring it to the LORD again. He is glad to be asked, and He goes out before His people (2 Samuel 5:24).
